analyst.summary: Ujjivan Small Finance Bank has come through a rough patch in its microfinance book and is now recovering well -- profit more than tripled year-on-year last quarter, asset quality has improved steadily, and loan growth is strong as the bank pushes into more secured lending. However, the RBI recently declined its application to become a full universal bank, citing continued reliance on microfinance, which removes a potential re-rating trigger for now. We rate it a Hold: a genuine recovery story, but not yet one that clears the bar for a stronger call.
